{{for|the Baer norm (intersection of normalizers)|Baer norm}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically [[abstract algebra]], if <math>(G, +)</math> is an ([[abelian group|abelian]]) [[Group_(mathematics)|group]] with identity element <math>e</math> then <math>\nu\colon G \to \mathbb{R}</math> is said to be a '''norm''' on <math>(G, +)</math> if:

#[[Positive definiteness]]: <math> \nu(g) > 0 \text{ for all } g \ne e \text{ and } \nu(e) = 0</math>,
#[[Subadditivity]]: <math> \nu(g+h) \le \nu(g) + \nu(h)</math>,
#Inversion (Symmetry): <math> \nu(-g) = \nu(g) \text{ for all } g \in G</math>.<ref name="BinghamOstaszewski">{{cite journal |last1=Bingham |first1=N.H. |last2=Ostaszewski |first2=A.J. |title=Normed versus topological groups: Dichotomy and duality |journal=Dissertationes Mathematicae |date=2010 |volume=472 |page=4|doi=10.4064/dm472-0-1 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Deza |first1=Michel |last2=Deza |first2=Elena |title=Encyclopedia of Distances |date=2016 |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |isbn=978-3-662-52844-0 |edition=4}}</ref>{{rp|§5 & §10.1}}

An alternative, stronger definition of a norm on <math>(G, +)</math> requires

#<math> \nu(g) > 0 \text{ for all } g \ne e</math>,
#<math> \nu(g+h) \le \nu(g) + \nu(h)</math>,
#<math> \nu(mg) = |m| \, \nu(g) \text{ for all } m \in \mathbb{Z}</math>.<ref name="Steprans">{{citation
 | last = Steprāns | first = Juris
 | doi = 10.2307/2044776
 | issue = 2
 | journal = [[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]
 | mr = 770551
 | pages = 347–349
 | title = A characterization of free abelian groups
 | volume = 93
 | year = 1985| jstor = 2044776
 }}</ref><ref name="Fuchs_2015">{{cite book |last1=Fuchs |first1=László |title=Abelian Groups |date=2015 |publisher=Springer |location=Cham |isbn=978-3-319-19422-6 |edition=1st |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-319-19422-6}}</ref>{{rp|§3.10}}

The norm <math>\nu</math> is '''discrete''' if there is some [[real number]] <math>\rho > 0</math> such that <math>\nu(g) > \rho</math> whenever <math>g \ne 0</math>.

== Free abelian groups ==
An abelian group is a [[free abelian group]] [[if and only if]] it has a discrete norm.<ref name="Steprans" /><ref name="Fuchs_2015" />{{rp|Th. 3.10.3}}
